messages.subject: Axis Limits
parts:
Hi. I am trying to control the axis limits and intervals on three different histograms so they are visually comparable. I want the x-axis to range from 0 to 15 with intervals of 1. I have used this -

a<-qplot(AchievementGapPoints, data = data, xlim = c(0,15), ylim = c(0,500), xlab = "Achievement Gap Points – Existing Rubric") + theme_bw() + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,15,1))

But if the data doesn't include values below 3, the scale is only showing 3-15. Does anyone know how to force it to show the 0-3 part? Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Axis Limits
parts:
See http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/scale_continuous.html

add geom

scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 15)) +

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: 6ed2ff7838c0c40e
messages.subject: Re: Axis Limits
parts:
One addendum to Roman's answer: If you use scale_x_continouous with a range that doesn't include the full range of the data, then ggplot will not only not plot the excluded data, it will also not include that data in any summary or percentage operations. To make sure all the data are always included, use coord_cartesian() to set axis limits. For example, compare the results of the following ggplot commands, which show how to set the axis limits (and tick locations) without unintentionally excluding data:

# Fake data
dat = data.frame(x=1:10, y=c(seq(10,90,10), 500))

# Basic scatterplot with linear regression line
ggplot(dat, aes(x,y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method='lm')

# Same, but with scale_x_continuous used to set x-limits. Note how the value at x=10, y=500 is excluded from the regression line due to "limits=c(0,9)" inside scale_x_continuous.
ggplot(dat, aes(x,y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method='lm') + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,10,1), limits=c(0,9))

# Using coord_cartesian gives you the x-limits you want in the graph, but without excluding data from the regression line
ggplot(dat, aes(x,y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method='lm') + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,10,1)) + coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,9))
